## Verdict

**Overall: FAIL for full compliance with the approved literal rule B.** The numerical rounding part of B and all of W pass. The additional emitter-tightness requirement in B fails: the outer graph bounds are approximately `4.18e-4` from the reported computed extrema, against the approved requirement of about `1e-6`. This discrepancy does **not** refute the Lean confinement theorem at 2.755%; it blocks an unqualified claim that the package satisfies the whole adopted rule B.

## Findings

### F1 — approved rule B's emitter tightness is not met

`docs/DECISIONS.md:326` (D40) records approval of all proposal recommendations and explicitly adopts rules B/W. `docs/tracks/SO/FREEZE-PROPOSAL-2.md:268–270` says:

> rule B also requires the emitter to set them within about 10⁻⁶ of the computed extrema, so that slack does not inflate δ.

The package's actual outer literals are `Data.Lower.cert.pLo = 0.9724531` and `Data.Upper.cert.pHi = 1.027544`. The generation evidence `g3/{lower,upper}_report.json`, field `graph_choice`, gives:

| Side | Reported grid extremum | Emitted bound | Gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lower bottom | 0.9728711380604858 | 0.9724531 | 0.0004180380604858 |
| upper top | 1.0271261674095928 | 1.027544 | 0.0004178325904072 |

The extrema here are numerical evidence, not certified extrema. The observation is about compliance with a rule explicitly referring to computed extrema. `scripts/spin_orbit/sofx_gen.py:104–142` explains the gap: subtract the SOS slack, then half the residual and outward rounding. The corresponding `m0` values are `0.972571138` and `-1.027426167`; residual halves are approximately `0.00011791008` and `0.00011766541`. Even the deliberate `3e-4` outer-side slack exceeds the requested tolerance. `docs/tracks/SO/studies/SO-V2PKG.md:258–260` independently acknowledges this numerical-versus-certified gap. The handoff lists the SOS margins as a deviation, but does not identify the resulting failure of this explicit rule-B clause. No replacement owner ruling was found in the controlling decisions.

Disposition: report the deviation for owner/orchestrator resolution before presenting these literals as fully rule-B-compliant or freezing them under D40. Improving the SOS enclosure or explicitly revising the requirement would resolve this contract issue. Do not silently replace the certified bound by a numerical grid extremum. No source or implementation repair was made in this audit.

### N1 — rounding formulas and band/window inequalities pass

Direct exact rational arithmetic on the Lean literals gives

```
M = max(1 - (9724531/10000000 - 578/10^13),
        (128443/125000 + 662/10^13) - 1)
  = 137734500289/5000000000000 = 0.0275469000578.
ceil(10^5 M)/10^5 = 2755/100000.
```

`lo = 97245/100000 = 1-δ` and `hi = 102755/100000 = 1+δ` are the required unreduced literals. The two band margins are `0.0000030999422` and `0.0000059999338`. Rule W gives exactly `9934/10000` and `10066/10000`: the nearest admissible four-decimal literals strictly inside the certified gap. Their margins are `0.0000741999422` and `0.0000820999338`. The next four-decimal literals towards the barriers fail the required strict inequalities. The five inequalities are actually proved by `lunarR2_band_ineqs`, not assumed by the final theorem.

The data use `err = 1.6e-16 / 1.83e-16` and `disp = 5.78e-11 / 6.62e-11`. The exact `disp_min` fractions in the existing `g2/witness.json` give approximately `5.776780851534296e-11` and `6.610712158003046e-11`; exact fraction comparison and upward three-significant-digit rounding give precisely the emitted displacements. Both clock coordinates are literally `(2000000/1000001, 0)`, equal to `(lunarR2Kappa, 0)`. Kernel-proved error/energy/invariance checks and refinedCore, rather than the generator's rounding prose, establish adequacy of the actual error/displacement values. The full mirror was not rerun.

## Statement and consumer audit

The barrier theorem has no input binders. Its witnesses are two `SoBarrier lo hi` values, with global ordering and strict placement on the two sides of the fixed window. `SoBarrier` is the existing structure of continuous, period-one invariant graphs, with both range bounds. The result does not assume barriers, certificate success, or a confinement conclusion.

The confinement theorem's binder accounting, relative to the handoff's exact Theorem B and FREEZE-PROPOSAL-2's approved global-solution scope:

| Expanded binder | Bin | Source / role |
|---|---|---|
| `q₀ : ℝ` | TYPING | Initial angle; handoff §1. |
| `p₀ : ℝ` | TYPING | Initial momentum; handoff §1. |
| `φ₀ : ℝ` | TYPING | Initial clock angle; handoff §1. |
| `hp.1 : lunarR2PLo < p₀` | SOURCE | Lower window condition. |
| `hp.2 : p₀ < lunarR2PHi` | SOURCE | Upper window condition. |

Counts: SOURCE 2, STANDING 0, TYPING 3, RULED 0, EXCESS 0. The barrier theorem has all five counts zero. Uniqueness quantifies over global differentiable solutions after exhibiting a single solution `z`; it does not claim an unrequested stronger local-solution uniqueness statement. Every real time, including negative time, is covered. The product coordinates are `(q,p,φ)` and the conclusion bounds `.2.1` about 1 by `δ`.

`LunarFinalR2V2.lean:53–60` supplies both data certificates, refined witnesses via `Sum.inr (Sum.inr ...)`, ham/parameter equalities, checker/graph success, frequency enclosures, and all five rational inequalities to `lunar_barriers_of_R2V2`. `LunarAssemblyV2.lean:75–99` discharges both actual N=65 Diophantine facts, γ comparisons, τ=1 and positive time scale. Its generic assembly calls the existing certified rotated-barrier construction and `soBarriers_of_band_rat`. `Graph/CertV2.lean:35–45` obtains the torus from `checkTorusCertificateV2_sound`; extracting the static check is legitimate conjunction elimination. `LunarFinalR2V2.lean:71–72` supplies the resulting barriers to the existing `lunar_spin_confinement_of_band`, plus the two rational band containments. These are actual term-level compositions, checked by the targeted build and exact-type probes.

Conditional computation lemmas deliberately take equalities/Bool successes as inputs. They have distinct helper names and are not used as substitute source theorems: the generated modules prove and supply every concrete premise. No new structure/typeclass bundles a desired conclusion. The complete local import closure of the final module contains 1,962 KAM modules, all 1,653 new Lean files, no provider and no frozen anchor. Frozen/provider signature and seal-copy probes therefore do not apply.

No new suspected mathematical defect in a pinned publication was identified in this package-level audit; existing analytic sources were not re-audited in full. F1 is a deviation from an adopted project specification, not a claim that the ODE theorem is false. The “five lines” width text is stale documentation; eight exact lines are exempted on inspected main. The planner change, per-side SOS slack, adapted formatters/mirror arithmetic, and the initial failed replay discovery attempts are explicitly retained as deviations/limitations rather than concealed.

The only repository deliverable is this report. No repairs, commits, root regeneration, frozen/provider changes, or source modifications were made. The report is complete even though its overall fidelity verdict is FAIL. Ordinary theorem validity at the emitted band is distinct from permission to freeze the band under the full approved rule B.

## Appendix A — complete declaration inventory

One row per new declaration, including finite data definitions and the private cast helper. Module headings identify the source path and namespace; the line column is the declaration's source line. `PASS` in this inventory means the computational/data or explicit conditional-assembly contract described above; it does not override F1 or certify a fresh source theorem for every datum. All 4,674 public theorem names were checked individually by the axiom probe. Closed generated proof families were reviewed through their source contracts, actual final consumption, static escape scan, and the prescribed kernel sample; the remaining heavy modules were not independently replayed wholesale. No claim of manually recomputing every data coefficient is made.

Axiom codes on each public theorem row: `A3` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, `A1` = `[propext]`, `A2` = `[propext, Quot.sound]`.

Kinds/bases: `LIT` = untrusted finite literal/input or proposed cached output, checked on use; `CODE` = total encoding/iteration/reflection algorithm; `EQ/ASM` = proved computation equality, Bool check, reflection, or explicitly conditional assembly; `CONST` = exact rational/backend literal; `F1` = literal policy limitation. Definition characterization and choice obligations are N/A_LITERAL/N/A as stated above.
